newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Arabia hopes to join WTO by 2002.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Arabia hopes to join WTO by 2002.

text.p: A Saudi official has predicted that the oil-rich kingdom would join the World Trade Organisation as an observer next year and become a full WTO member by the year 2002, the Saudi Press Agency (SPA) said on Sunday.

The official agency quoted Ismael Abu Daoud, chairman of the board of trustees of the Jedda Chamber of Commerce and Industry, as saying that negotiations between Saudi Arabia and the WTO were going smoothly.
"He asserted that the negotiations between the kingdom and the organisation were being conducted in a studied manner and that there were no difficulties facing the negotiations," SPA said.
It said Abu Daoud explained that Saudi Arabia was adapting its economy, trade and regulations to suit WTO laws.
But the agency said Abu Daoud indicated that Saudi Arabia had expressed reservations on specific issues still under discussion. It did not elaborate.

Saudi Arabia, the world's largest oil producer, applied to join the trade watchdog's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in 1993. They have held three rounds of talks since 1993.
Trade diplomats reported progress in the discussions after the third round of talks in May but said Saudi Arabia must do more to present detailed offers on market access.

Concerns among the trading partners include Saudi Arabia's restrictions on import licensing in areas such as chemicals, pasteurised milk, information technology products, agricultural equipment and machinery.
